title: A section vanishing on the fibre vanishes after pointed refinement
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative ring and F a sheaf of Lambda-modules on the small etale site of a scheme X [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let f:X -> Y be integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let s:Spec Omega -> Y be a geometric point with Omega algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and let (g':X' -> X,f':X' -> Spec Omega,f,s) be Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. For a pointed etale neighbourhood (V,v), define R_(V,v):F(V times_Y X) -> Gamma(X',g'^*F) as the inverse-image unit for g' restricted along the iterated pullback lift with first projection (f' followed by v,g') and second projection the identity of X'. For every V,v,z with R_(V,v)(z)=0 there exist a pointed etale neighbourhood (W,w) and a map a:W -> V over Y taking w to v, such that the restriction of z along a times_Y X is zero.

proof.text: Restrict to an affine neighbourhood of s and form the strict henselization Spec A. Integrality makes its pullback Spec B affine and B integral over A. Use the canonical underlying-set inverse-image comparison, including the unit equation, to apply the set-valued stalk formula to the module sheaf F. The local-structure theorem makes the chosen ring-colimit A strictly henselian, so its residue field is separably closed.

Let m be the maximal ideal of A. The integral henselian-pair theorem makes (B,mB) henselian. Apply henselian degree-zero comparison to the proper identity of Spec B. Further restriction from the separably closed residue field of A to Omega is bijective on sections. Composition of units and the two pullback projections identify the resulting restriction with R_(V,v).

The two injective restriction maps force the strict-henselization image of z to be zero. The stalk comparison is injective, so the germ of z is zero. Apply Point.toPresheafFiber_eq_iff' to the germ equality with zero; since restriction is linear, the resulting pointed refinement W -> V kills z. Affine cofinality permits the refinement to map to the original V even if V was not affine. The empty fibre is also covered; alternatively, shrink the base away from the closed integral image.

lean.statement:
theorem integralFibreSection_localZero
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {X' X Y : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of Ω)} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f s) [IsIntegralHom f]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (V : Y.Etale) (v : (pointSmallEtale s).fiber.obj V)
    (z : F.obj.obj (op (f.Etale.obj V)))
    (hz : (geometricFibreSectionRestriction Λ sq.toCommSq F V v).hom z = 0) :
    ∃ (W : Y.Etale) (w : (pointSmallEtale s).fiber.obj W) (a : W ⟶ V),
      (pointSmallEtale s).fiber.map a w = v ∧
        (F.obj.map (f.Etale.map a).op).hom z = 0
